title: ImageJ Fluorescence Image Composition
author: Kenneth Schackart
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yc8fszw

steps.title: Download and install ImageJ
steps.instruction: Visit https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/download.html, select the version for your operating system, download the software, and install it according to the provided installer instructions.

steps.title: Launch ImageJ if not auto‑detected
steps.instruction: If ImageJ does not appear in your program list, manually navigate to the folder where you installed it and open the executable file.

steps.title: Open images to be merged
steps.instruction: Load each fluorescence image into ImageJ either by dragging the file onto the ImageJ window or by choosing File → Open and selecting the files.

steps.title: Convert images to 8‑bit
steps.instruction: For each opened image, click on the image window, then select Image → Type → 8‑bit to change its type to 8‑bit. Verify that the image type now reads 8‑bit.

steps.title: Merge channels
steps.instruction: Select Image → Color → Merge Channels… to open the Merge Channels dialog.

steps.title: Assign channel colors
steps.instruction: In the Merge Channels dialog, assign each image to a color channel using the drop‑down menus: Red → TRITC, Green → FITC, Blue → DAPI.

steps.title: Create merged image
steps.instruction: Press OK in the Merge Channels dialog; ImageJ will generate a merged composite image.

steps.title: Enhance image contrast
steps.instruction: To improve visibility, select Process → Enhance Contrast… and apply the default settings (or adjust as needed) to the merged image.
